# 2 Maccabees Chapter 14 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 2 Maccabees 14 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/2MA_014_page_001.jpg

---

**14:1** After a period of three years, it was reported to Judas and his men that Demetrius the son of Seleucus, having sailed into the harbor of Tripolis with a strong army and a fleet,

**14:2** had seized the kingdom, after doing away with Antiochus and his guardian Lysias.

**14:3** Now one Alcimus, who had been high priest and had willfully defiled himself in the times of separation, considering that there was no way for him to be safe and that he would have no more access to the holy altar,

**14:4** came to King Demetrius in the year one hundred fifty-one, bringing him a crown of gold and a palm branch, and besides these some of the customary olive branches from the temple. And for that day he held his peace.

**14:5** But having found a good opportunity for his mad purpose, when he was invited by Demetrius into the council and was asked about the dispositions and intentions of the Jews, he answered:

**14:6** "Those of the Jews who are called Hasideans, whose leader is Judas Maccabeus, are keeping up war and stirring up sedition, and will not let the kingdom attain tranquility.

**14:7** Therefore I have been deprived of my ancestral glory — I mean the high priesthood — and have come here,

**14:8** first because I genuinely care for the interests of the king, and second because I have regard also for my own countrymen; for through the folly of those whom I mentioned our whole nation is in no small trouble.

**14:9** Therefore, O king, having informed yourself of all these things, take thought for our country and for our nation, which is surrounded on all sides, according to the gracious kindness that you show to all.

**14:10** For as long as Judas is alive, it is impossible for the government to find peace."

**14:11** When he had said these things, the rest of the king's friends, who were hostile to Judas, quickly inflamed Demetrius further.

**14:12** And immediately he appointed Nicanor, who had been in command of the elephants, as governor of Judea, and sent him off

**14:13** with orders to kill Judas and scatter his men and to install Alcimus as high priest of the great temple.

**14:14** And the Gentiles throughout Judea who had fled before Judas began to flock to Nicanor, thinking that the misfortunes and calamities of the Jews would be their own gain.

**14:15** When the Jews heard of Nicanor's coming and the gathering of the Gentiles, they sprinkled earth upon their heads and petitioned him who had established his people for all time and who always comes to the aid of his inheritance by manifestation.

**14:16** At the order of their leader they set out immediately from that place and engaged them at a village called Dessau.

**14:17** Simon, the brother of Judas, had engaged Nicanor, but had suffered a temporary check because of the sudden appearance of the enemy.

**14:18** Nevertheless Nicanor, hearing of the valor of Judas and his men and their courage in battle for their fatherland, was afraid to decide the matter by bloodshed.

**14:19** Therefore he sent Posidonius and Theodotus and Mattathias to give and receive pledges of friendship.

**14:20** When the terms had been fully considered, and the leader had informed the multitude, and it had appeared that they were of one mind, they consented to the covenants.

**14:21** And they set a day on which to meet privately. A litter was brought forward from each side; they placed chairs of state.

**14:22** Judas posted armed men in readiness at key places, lest suddenly the enemy should spring a plot. They held the meeting in a fitting manner.

**14:23** Nicanor stayed on in Jerusalem and did nothing out of the way but dismissed the crowds that had gathered to him.

**14:24** And he kept Judas always at his side; he was warmly attached to the man.

**14:25** He urged him to marry and have children; he married, was well settled, and shared in the common life.

**14:26** But Alcimus, noticing the goodwill between them and taking hold of the covenants that had been made, came to Demetrius and told him that Nicanor was disloyal to the government, since he had appointed as his successor in affairs Judas, a conspirator against the kingdom.

**14:27** The king became excited and, infuriated by the false accusations of that most wicked man, wrote to Nicanor stating that he was displeased at the covenants and commanding him to send Maccabeus to Antioch as a prisoner without delay.

**14:28** When this news reached Nicanor, he was troubled and was grieved that he had to annul their agreements when the man had done no wrong.

**14:29** But since it was not possible to act contrary to the king, he watched for an opportunity to carry out this order by a stratagem.

**14:30** Maccabeus noticed that Nicanor was behaving more austerely toward him and was acting more rudely than usual in their meetings, and concluded that this austerity was not for the good. So he gathered a large number of his men and went into hiding from Nicanor.

**14:31** When the latter recognized that he had been outstandingly outwitted by the man, he went to the great and holy temple while the priests were offering the customary sacrifices, and commanded them to hand the man over.

**14:32** When they declared on oath that they did not know where the man was whom he sought,

**14:33** he stretched out his right hand toward the sanctuary and swore this oath: "If you do not hand Judas over to me as a prisoner, I will level this sanctuary of God to the ground and tear down the altar, and I will erect here a splendid temple to Dionysus."

**14:34** Having said these things he departed. But the priests stretched out their hands toward heaven and called upon him who always fights on behalf of our nation, saying:

**14:35** "You, O Lord of all, who have need of nothing, were pleased to have a temple for your dwelling in our midst.

**14:36** So now, O holy one, Lord of all holiness, keep undefiled for all time this house that has so recently been purified."

**14:37** A certain Razis, one of the elders of Jerusalem, was denounced to Nicanor as a man who loved his fellow countrymen and was well regarded and who for his goodwill was called father of the Jews.

**14:38** For in the former times, when there was no mingling, he had been accused of Judaism and had submitted his body and soul in full earnestness to Judaism.

**14:39** Nicanor, wishing to exhibit openly his ill will toward the Jews, sent more than five hundred soldiers to arrest him.

**14:40** For he thought that by arresting him he would deal a blow to the Jews.

**14:41** Now when the troops were on the point of capturing the tower and were forcing the door of the courtyard, and the order had been given to set fire to the door, he was surrounded on all sides. Having drawn his sword,

**14:42** he chose rather to die nobly than to fall into the hands of sinners and suffer outrages unworthy of his noble birth.

**14:43** But missing his stroke because of the rush of the moment, with the crowd pressing in through the doors, he ran boldly up to the wall and threw himself down bravely into the crowd.

**14:44** But when they quickly drew back, a space was made and he came down in the middle.

**14:45** Still breathing, and inflamed in spirit, he rose up; and with blood gushing out in streams and with grievous wounds, he ran through the crowd. And standing on a steep rock,

**14:46** with his blood now almost completely drained, he tore out his entrails, and taking them in both hands he hurled them at the crowd. And calling upon the Lord of life and spirit to restore them to him again, he died in this way.
